The **climate of Mumbai** is [tropical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropical_climate "Tropical climate") , with defined wet and dry seasons ( [Köppen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Köppen_climate_classification "Köppen climate classification") : _[Aw](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropical_savanna_climate "Tropical savanna climate") / [Am](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropical_monsoon_climate "Tropical monsoon climate")_ ). The mean annual temperature is 27\.7 °C or 81.9 °F . Average annual rainfall is 2,213.4 millimetres or 87 inches in Colaba, which represents South Mumbai, and 2,502.3 millimetres or 99 inches in Santacruz, which represents central and suburban Mumbai. [[ 1 ]](:2-1) The mean maximum average temperatures is about 32 °C (90 °F) in summer and 30 °C (86 °F) in winter, while the average minimums are 26 °C (79 °F) in summer and 18 °C (64 °F) in winter. The city experiences a lengthy, practically rainless [dry season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dry_season "Dry season") , and a relatively short, but extremely rainy [wet season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wet_season "Wet season") ; due to [the Southwest Monsoon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monsoon_of_South_Asia "Monsoon of South Asia") and orographic influences from the nearby [Western Ghats](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Western_Ghats "Western Ghats") .These conditions effectively place Mumbai between a [Tropical monsoon climate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropical_monsoon_climate "Tropical monsoon climate") ( [Am](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropical_monsoon_climate "Tropical monsoon climate") ) and a [Tropical savannah climate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropical_savannah_climate "Tropical savannah climate") ( [Aw](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropical_savannah_climate "Tropical savannah climate") ), with more tilt towards the former considering annual precipitation.

## Monthly breakdown of climate

[ [edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Climate_of_Mumbai&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Monthly breakdown of climate") ]

The following is the monthly breakdown of the weather in Mumbai.

### January

[ [edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Climate_of_Mumbai&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: January") ]

January is the coolest month of the year for Mumbai, with the mean daily minimum being 16.4 °C and the mean daily maximum being 30.1 °C. [[ 11 ]]() [[ 12 ]]() The nightly lows may vary between 13 °C and 20 °C. Chilly northern winds during the day make the city seem cooler than it is. Generally, clear skies, with some [smog](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smog "Smog") – especially in the early morning – are the norm. The days are dry, and the nights relatively [humid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Humid "Humid") . January is also associated with the [deciduous](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deciduous "Deciduous") trees in the city shedding their leaves. On 26–27 January 2008, recorded a minimum temperature of 10.2 °C, which is the lowest recorded in 45 years. The lowest recorded temperature is 7.4 °C (45.3 °F) on 22 January 1962, which was the coldest day in Mumbai. Coastal areas are relatively cooler during the day, but they are warmer at night.

### February

[ [edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Climate_of_Mumbai&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: February") ]

The fine January weather continues for the first fortnight of February. The mean daily minimum stays at 17.3 °C and the mean daily maximum is 31.3 °C with some possibility of unseasonable showers. [[ 11 ]]() Smog increases. 6 February 2008 recorded a minimum temperature of 9.4 °C. Just two days later, on 8 February, the minimum temperature recorded was 8.5 °C, which was the lowest temperature Mumbai had seen since January 1962. [[ 13 ]]()

### March

[ [edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Climate_of_Mumbai&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: March") ]

The month of March sees a mean minimum temp of 20.6 °C and a mean maximum temp of 32.7 °C. [[ 11 ]]() During the transition from dry to humid weather in mid-March, the temperature might hit 38 to 40 °C. This high, however, is due to hot dry winds from [Gujarat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gujarat "Gujarat") . By mid-March the temperatures may hit 37 °C, with the lows at 24 °C. Humidity is unbearable, and smog affects the city. New leaves sprout from deciduous trees. The all-time high day temperature for March was recorded in 2018 at 41.7 °C. [[ 14 ]]()

### April

[ [edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Climate_of_Mumbai&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: April") ]

The temperatures and humidity are still high. However, the cooling effect of the sea breezes makes its presence felt. The high temperature stays around 35.1 °C and daily lows are around 23.2 °C. Plants are in full bloom in April.

### May

[ [edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Climate_of_Mumbai&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: May") ]

May is the hottest month of the year for Mumbai with the cool sea breezes providing some relief. The daily maximum hovers around 34.5 °C and the daily low is 29.1 °C. [[ 11 ]]()

### June

[ [edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Climate_of_Mumbai&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: June") ]

June marks the beginning of the [monsoon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monsoon "Monsoon") period in [Mumbai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mumbai "Mumbai") . The beginning of the month is characterized by a continuation of the summer with increased [humidity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Humidity "Humidity") . The official date for the monsoon to hit the city is 10 June. [[ 15 ]]() This period is marked by [thunderstorms](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thunderstorms "Thunderstorms") and often windy conditions as the monsoon establishes itself over the city. Rainfall activity intensifies as the month goes on, leading into the wettest month, July. The max and min mean daily temperatures are measured at 34.5 °C/26.6 °C. [[ 11 ]]()

### July

[ [edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Climate_of_Mumbai&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: July") ]

[](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Mumbai_monsoon.jpg) Waterlogging due to showers

In this month the city receives the maximum amount of [rain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rain "Rain") . July and August are characterized by almost non-stop rain and weeks of no sunshine. A continuous [monsoon current](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monsoon_current?action=edit&redlink=1 "Monsoon current (page does not exist)") covers the entire [western coast of India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Western_coast_of_India?action=edit&redlink=1 "Western coast of India (page does not exist)") during this period. Rainfall activity is less stormy and more constant with a relatively constant breeze from the West or South West. It is not uncommon for parts of the city to be waterlogged during periods of persistent heavy rain. This affects the city's public transport system often leading to long delays. During periods of severe [precipitation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Precipitation "Precipitation") , the city's commuter rail system is often suspended because of water logging and poor visibility.

The average maximum temperature for the month is around 29.8 °C with the average minimum at 25.5 °C. [[ 11 ]]() Average monthly rainfall is 919.9 mm in Santacruz and 768.5 mm in Colaba. [[ 1 ]](:2-1) The highest 24-hour rainfall in the history of Mumbai was recorded at the Santacruz observatory of the [India Meteorological Department](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/India_Meteorological_Department "India Meteorological Department") on 26 July 2005. On this day, a [record 944 mm rainfall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maharashtra_floods_of_2005 "Maharashtra floods of 2005") fell over the city, causing large-scale flooding, claiming several lives and causing large-scale [property damage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Property_damage "Property damage") . [[ 16 ]]()

### August

[ [edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Climate_of_Mumbai&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: August") ]

The weather in August is almost identical to July. Towards the latter half of the month, rainfall activity tends to lessen. The coolest days of the monsoon season are often in August. The max temperature might drop to 29.3 °C during the day and 24.5 °C at night. [[ 11 ]]()

### September

[ [edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Climate_of_Mumbai&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: September") ]

In September the intensity of rainfall decreases. The monsoons officially end in the 3rd week of September. September has unsettled weather. The rainfall is short and light and is not continuous. The end of the monsoon, much like the beginning can feature heavy thunderstorms associated with the withdrawal of the monsoon current from the city and surrounding areas. The mean maximum daily temperatures reach 30.1 °C while daily mean minimum temperature stays at 24.0 °C. [[ 11 ]]()

### October

[ [edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Climate_of_Mumbai&action=edit&section=13 "Edit section: October") ]

In the month of October, the mean daily maximum stays at around 32.9 °C and the mean daily minimum stays at 23.1 °C [[ 11 ]]() making it hot during the days and relatively mild during the nights.

### November

[ [edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Climate_of_Mumbai&action=edit&section=14 "Edit section: November") ]

The temperature continues to drop slowly in the month of November with the mean daily minimum staying at 20.5 °C and the mean daily maximum staying around 33.4 °C. [[ 11 ]]() There are a few unseasonable showers.

### December

[ [edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Climate_of_Mumbai&action=edit&section=15 "Edit section: December") ]

The day highs hover around 32.4 °C. The nights average around 18.2 °C. [[ 11 ]]() Humidity is low in December.

## Climate change

[ [edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Climate_of_Mumbai&action=edit&section=16 "Edit section: Climate change") ]

As climate change and global warming are issues of rapidly increasing importance, the Mumbai Government launched the [Mumbai Climate Action Plan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mumbai_Climate_Action_Plan "Mumbai Climate Action Plan") to tackle climate change and extreme weather events. [[ 17 ]]()

## Cyclones in Mumbai

[ [edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Climate_of_Mumbai&action=edit&section=17 "Edit section: Cyclones in Mumbai") ]

Sitting on the coast, Mumbai is vulnerable to cyclones, but as the cyclones in the Arabian Sea turn to the Arabian Peninsula or Gujarat, Mumbai stands less affected. [[ 18 ]]() Cyclones that have affected Mumbai include 1618, [[ 19 ]](:1-19) 1698, [[ 19 ]](:1-19) 1702, [[ 19 ]](:1-19) 1740, [[ 19 ]](:1-19) 1742, [[ 19 ]](:1-19) 1762, [[ 19 ]](:1-19) 1799, [[ 19 ]](:1-19) 1854, [[ 19 ]](:1-19) 1882 ( [which is believed to be a hoax](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bombay_Cyclone_of_1882 "Bombay Cyclone of 1882") ), 1891 [[ 20 ]]() 1940 [[ 21 ]](:0-21) [1948](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1940s_North_Indian_Ocean_cyclone_seasons "1940s North Indian Ocean cyclone seasons") , [[ 22 ]]() [Cyclone Phyan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cyclone_Phyan "Cyclone Phyan") , [[ 23 ]]() [Cyclone Ockhi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cyclone_Ockhi "Cyclone Ockhi") , [[ 24 ]]() [Cyclone Vayu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cyclone_Vayu "Cyclone Vayu") , [[ 25 ]]() [Cyclone Nisarga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cyclone_Nisarga "Cyclone Nisarga") , [[ 21 ]](:0-21) and [Cyclone Tauktae](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cyclone_Tauktae "Cyclone Tauktae") . [[ 26 ]]()

The strongest cyclone ever recorded to hit Mumbai is the 1948 Mumbai Cyclone, which hit the city on November 21, 1948. Gusts in [Juhu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juhu "Juhu") reached 151 km/h; torrential rains lashed the city, reaching 5 inches in only 24 hours. Flooding occurred due to heavy rains, and the city power supply was disrupted. The cyclone left 38 people dead and 47 missing. Local transport came to a standstill. [[ 21 ]](:0-21) [[ 22 ]]() [[ 27 ]]() [[ 28 ]]()

In 2021, [Cyclone Tauktae](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cyclone_Tauktae "Cyclone Tauktae") battered Mumbai, reaching gusts of 114 km/h with heavy rains. The storm was catastrophic, and flight operations at Mumbai's Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj International Airport halted for hours due to the cyclone. [[ 29 ]]() [[ 30 ]]()
